title.text: Manila Southwoods Golf and Country Club

title_en.text: Manila Southwoods Golf and Country Club

tagline.text: A members' club with 36 Nicklaus-designed holes in Carmona

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: One day (about 5 hours of golf plus travel)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: From about ₱10,750 (tourist program for non-residents, 18 holes per person)

children.text: This members' golf club in Carmona, Cavite, south of Manila, has 36 holes designed by Jack Nicklaus. Non-resident foreign visitors can play the Legends Course on weekdays through the club's tourist program.

Manila Southwoods Golf and Country Club is a members' golf club inside the Southwoods estate in Carmona, Cavite. It has two 18-hole courses designed by Jack Nicklaus, the Legends and the Masters, for 36 holes in all, and both are par 72. According to Wikipedia, the Legends Course opened on July 26, 1992, and the Masters Course followed the next year. The club hosted the Philippine Open in 1993, 1994, 1996 and 1999, and the tournament returned here in 2025, which makes it one of the country's best-known tournament venues.

First, a point to keep in mind: this is basically a members' club. It is not a public course where anyone can book with a single phone call. However, the club's official website has a separate tourist program, and foreigners who do not reside in the Philippines can play the Legends Course on weekdays. The conditions are non-resident status, Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays), tee-off at
or later, and the Legends Course only. The fee is

per person, which covers an 18-hole green fee, a caddie fee (tips not included) and a cart shared by two players. Expats living in the Philippines, including permanent residents and long-term visa holders, are not eligible for this program and would need to play as a member or a member's guest.

The two courses have quite different characters. According to a July 2025 article on the travel site Primer, the Masters Course measures about 7,168 yards, has many water hazards, and is known for its island green on the 9th hole. The Legends Course measures about 7,058 yards, with wider fairways and fewer hazards, so it is relatively forgiving. GolfPass lists the Legends Course at 6,566 m from the championship tees, with a course rating of 73.6 and a slope of 136. Top100GolfCourses describes the Legends Course as the easier of the two and calls the long par-5 17th one of the toughest par fives in the country. The Legends Course is the one you can play through the tourist program.
The club's own directions say the drive down SLEX (the South Luzon Expressway) from Manila takes about
30 minutes

. That figure is from Makati, and it can take much longer during rush hour. Plan on spending a full day at the course. This guide focuses on how visitors (non-members) can actually play, and since fees and rules change often, be sure to confirm the latest details with the club when you book. For a first visit, here is a sensible way to prepare. Two to three weeks before your trip, call or email the club's front desk with your preferred weekday, group size, nationality and residency status, and check tee-time availability. Then ask in one go about the final fee and payment method, caddie tipping customs, whether rental clubs are available, and the dress code, which spares you surprises on the day. Booking through a travel agency is convenient because hotel pickup and reservations are bundled, but the price for the same program can differ, so compare it with the club's official rate. A round on a par-72 course typically takes four to five hours, and with travel time included it is realistic to plan it as a full-day outing.
Both the Legends and the Masters were designed by Jack Nicklaus and play to par 72. Few places in the Philippines have 36 Nicklaus signature holes, which makes this a destination for golf trips.

blocks.title: Tourist round on the Legends Course

children.text: Non-resident foreigners can play the Legends Course on weekdays with a tee-off at 10:00 AM or later. The 18-hole green fee, caddie and a cart shared by two are bundled into a single price, which keeps the math simple.
The Philippine Open was held here in 1993, 1994, 1996 and 1999, and the tournament returned in 2025. Playing a course that has hosted professional events is a big part of the appeal.

blocks.title: The island green on the Masters Course

children.text: The Masters Course has many water hazards and is known for the island green on the 9th hole. You cannot play it through the tourist program, but if you can get a round as a member's guest, it is worth a try.

The Legends Course has wide fairways and few trees, so the ball moves around a lot when the wind blows. Visitor reviews repeatedly describe the greens as fast and firm. Some putting practice beforehand helps.

There is a Legends clubhouse, a Masters clubhouse and a separate sports club. They are convenient for a meal or a shower before or after your round. Primer says the on-site restaurant Le Chef serves Filipino comfort food and international dishes.
From the SLEX Carmona exit, the club entrance is about
4km
away, so a day trip from central Manila is possible. The club says it is about 30 minutes from Makati.

items.title: One-day round
items.subtitle: From Manila to 18 holes on the Legends Course

children.text: Leave your hotel in Manila (Makati or BGC). It is best to set out early to avoid the SLEX morning traffic. If you use a travel agency package, hotel pickup is included.

Exit SLEX at Carmona, turn right onto Governor's Drive, and after about 3 km turn right again onto Southwoods Boulevard. The club entrance is about 1 km further. You will be checked in at the entrance.
Check in at the front desk and pay the tourist program fee. You will be assigned a caddie, and you can locate the lockers and showers.
Tourist tee times start at 10:00 AM. Start from the 1st hole of the Legends Course at your booked time.
After your round, shower and eat at the clubhouse. The caddie tip is not included in the fee, so bring cash in advance.
Head back to Manila. SLEX is congested during the evening rush, so leave yourself some margin.
This schedule is an example, and the club sets the actual tee time when you book.
Take SLEX and exit at Carmona. The club's official directions say it is about 30 minutes from Makati.
From the exit, turn right onto Governor's Drive, and after about 3 km turn right onto Southwoods Boulevard.
Follow Southwoods Boulevard for about 1 km to reach the club entrance. The address is 1 Southwoods Avenue, Carmona, Cavite 4116.
SLEX congestion at rush hour makes the trip much longer. Check the latest travel time on a map app.
You can go by Grab, taxi or a rental car with a driver. For a golf-specific pickup service, the most reliable answer is to ask the club.
Some travel agency tourist program packages include hotel pickup in Manila and a driver. What is included differs by operator, so check before you book.
You can play golf year-round, but the dry season from November to May is the most comfortable. December to February is relatively cool and ideal for a round.
June to October is the rainy season, with afternoon showers and thunder on many days. Booking a morning tee time is safer, and play can be suspended when a lightning warning is issued.

The club has a Legends clubhouse and a Masters clubhouse, and Primer says the restaurant Le Chef serves Filipino comfort food and international dishes. Eating at the clubhouse after your round is the easiest option. Among the dishes mentioned, beef tapa was ₱380.

Most visitors stay in a Manila hotel (Makati or BGC) and make it a day trip. If you want to stay near Carmona, ask the club or a travel agency whether a stay-and-play package exists. This guide could not confirm whether the club has on-site accommodation.

Reservations are made through the club's front desk. The official page says bookings are accepted by phone, fax or email. The front desk number is +63 917 502 0784, the Cavite line is (046) 419 8190 ext. 140/141, and the Manila line is (02) 7795 5900 ext. 140/141.
The tourist program is open only to foreign non-residents of the Philippines. Bring your passport and entry records, and residents should look into playing as a member's guest.
Tee-off is at
or later on weekdays. The tourist program does not run on weekends or public holidays.
A dress code applies. GolfPass states that proper golf attire is required, so bring a collared shirt and golf shoes.

The caddie tip is separate and paid in cash. One travel booking site recommends about ₱300 per 18 holes, while another travel agency lists a minimum of US$20 per caddie, so guidance differs widely (roughly ₱300 to US$20). Amounts can change, so confirm with the club.
The Legends Course has few trees, so it is strongly affected by wind, and the greens are fast. Get used to the speed on the putting green before your round.
Some operators say rental clubs are available, but stock is limited and you must request them in advance. Bringing your own clubs is safer.
Fees and rules change often. Confirm the latest fee and rules with the club before you book.

Leave time to warm up before your round. A travel agency source mentions a driving range at the club, so if you want to practice about an hour before your tee time, ask the club in advance about availability and fees.
This is a members' club, and the tourist program is open only to foreign non-residents of the Philippines, on weekdays, on the Legends Course only.
Residents of the Philippines cannot use the tourist program, so be sure to confirm your eligibility before booking.
The rate on the official page (
) carries no date. Older sources show lower figures such as
, so confirm the latest rate by phone.

One visitor review from February 2026 reported that the course was in poor shape and had temporary tees (though the greens were good and quick). Older reviews from 2016 and 2019 described good conditions, so opinions vary by period. Ask about course conditions and the Masters Course maintenance schedule.
In the rainy season, play can be suspended by lightning, and SLEX is heavily congested on weekday afternoons. Leave plenty of time for your return.
You are checked in at the estate entrance. Bring your booking confirmation.
